meta.titre: Mass Movements and Slope Processes: why slopes fail and how the losses are reduced

sections.contenu_markdown: In the rainy season, hillside neighbourhoods and farms in many parts of Cameroon sit on ground that can suddenly slide downhill, burying houses, crops and roads. Rain is only the trigger: the angle of the slope, the strength of the ground, the water it holds, the vegetation and human activity all decide whether it holds. Examiners regularly ask for the effects of landslides on people, the ways of preventing them and the best way to cut losses. This course gives you the types of movement, a simple stability calculation and a method for impact and prevention questions.

items: Weathering breaks rock down in place and produces regolith and soil.
Gravity pulls every mass on a slope downhill, and the pull has a component parallel to the slope.
Water in the ground fills the pore spaces between grains.
Cohesion and friction between grains resist movement of soil and rock.

sections.titre: Mass movement: types, causes, stability and control
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Definitions
- **Mass movement** (mass wasting) is the downslope movement of rock, regolith or soil under gravity, without a moving agent such as a river or glacier carrying the material. Water often helps the movement but does not transport the mass.
- **Landslide** is the general term for a mass of rock, debris or earth moving down a slope.

### Main types
| Type | Style of movement | Typical setting |
|---|---|---|
| Rockfall | Blocks fall freely or bounce down a steep face | Jointed rock in cliffs and road cuttings |
| Rock slide | A slab slides on a flat surface such as a bedding plane or joint | Beds dip out of the slope |
| Rotational slump | A block moves on a curved surface and tilts backwards, leaving a scarp | Weak clay or thick wet soil |
| Debris flow or mudflow | Saturated soil and debris flow like a thick fluid | Steep slopes, heavy rain, little vegetation |
| Soil creep | Very slow surface movement, shown by leaning poles and bent tree trunks | Gentle to moderate slopes |

### Stability and the factor of safety
A slope fails when the driving force exceeds the resisting force. The **factor of safety** is the resisting force (shear strength) divided by the driving force (shear stress), and failure occurs when $FS < 1$. For a slab of weight $W$ on a plane of angle $\theta$, with base area $A$, cohesion $c$, friction angle $\varphi$ and water uplift force $U$:

$$
FS = \frac{cA + (W\cos\theta - U)\tan\varphi}{W\sin\theta}
$$

- **Driving forces rise** with steeper slopes (undercutting by rivers, road cuts, quarries), extra load (buildings, fill, water) and earthquake vibration.
- **Resisting forces fall** when water raises pore-water pressure, when weathering weakens the rock, when deforestation removes binding roots, and where weak clay layers or planes dipping out of the slope are present.

### Impacts and control
- **Impacts**: deaths and injuries; homes, farms, roads and pipes destroyed; roads cut so that villages lose access to markets; lost income and displacement; silted streams and lost topsoil.
- **Prevention (reduces the chance of failure)**: drainage, regrading and terracing, replanting, retaining walls, gabions and rock bolts.
- **Minimising impacts (reduces exposure)**: land-use zoning, no building on unstable slopes, monitoring, warning systems, public education and evacuation plans.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is outline, state or list and each point earns one mark.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write short, separate points, grouped as human, economic and environmental, and tie each to a livelihood: a farmer's crop buried, a trader unable to reach market because a road is cut, a family that loses its home and savings, a village without a water pipe. One clear, specific point earns one mark, so avoid long explanations and do not repeat the same idea in different words.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how landslides can be prevented or controlled.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the method and say how it works in the same sentence, for example: horizontal drains remove groundwater, lower pore-water pressure and raise the factor of safety. A bare list of names scores poorly. Group the methods: reduce driving forces (regrade the slope, remove load), increase resisting forces (retaining walls, rock bolts, roots) and remove water (surface ditches and subsurface drains).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the most effective way to minimise the impacts or losses.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Separate hazard reduction from exposure reduction. A wall or terrace protects only the slope where it is built and needs money and maintenance. Education, warning systems, evacuation plans and keeping people and buildings off unstable ground reduce losses across a whole district. When the question is about the impact on people, the option that changes where people live and how they react is usually the stronger answer.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain why a steep, deforested hillside is more likely to fail after several days of heavy rain than the same hillside under forest, and state two measures that would improve its stability. (6 marks)

etapes.justification: Explain asks for reasons linked by cause and effect, and there are two tasks: why the failure happens and two measures.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: (1) role of vegetation, (2) role of water, (3) link to the factor of safety, (4) two measures.

etapes.justification: The question contrasts forest with a deforested slope, so the difference must come first.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Roots bind the soil and add cohesion, leaves intercept rain and plants take water from the ground. Removing them leaves weaker soil that receives and keeps more water.

etapes.justification: Rain is the trigger, so the mechanism must be given and not only the word rain.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Infiltration saturates the soil, pore-water pressure rises and pushes grains apart, friction falls, and the water adds weight to the slope.

etapes.justification: The factor of safety shows why the slope fails and not only that it does.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Strength falls and the downslope force rises, so $FS = \text{resisting force} / \text{driving force}$ drops below 1; on a steep slope the downslope component of weight is already large, so the margin is small.

etapes.action: Give two measures with how they work.
etapes.justification: A measure without its mechanism earns no mark.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Drains and ditches carry water away and lower pore-water pressure; replanting deep-rooted trees restores root cohesion and reduces infiltration.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** Deforestation removes the roots that bind the soil and the leaves that intercept rain, so more water enters the slope. After several days of rain the soil is saturated, pore-water pressure rises and pushes the grains apart, which lowers the friction holding the slope together, while the extra weight of water increases the downslope force. On a steep slope the factor of safety, resisting force divided by driving force, then falls below 1 and the slope fails. Stability can be improved by drainage ditches and drains, which lower pore-water pressure, and by replanting deep-rooted trees, which restore root cohesion and reduce infiltration.

items.erreur_markdown: Landslides are caused by heavy rain only.
items.pourquoi_faux: Rain is the trigger, but the slope angle, weak material, planes dipping out of the slope and loss of vegetation are the conditions that make failure possible. The same rain on a gentle, well-vegetated slope may cause nothing.
items.correction_markdown: Write that rain triggers failure on slopes already made unstable by steepness, weak material or lost vegetation.

items.erreur_markdown: A mudflow is erosion by a river because it contains water.
items.pourquoi_faux: Mass movement is driven by gravity. The water lowers friction, but the mixture of soil and water moves as a dense flow and is not carried by a stream.
items.correction_markdown: Describe a mudflow as a gravity-driven flow of saturated debris, which is a mass movement and not river transport.

items.erreur_markdown: Water makes the slope slippery, and that is its only effect.
items.pourquoi_faux: Lubrication is a weak explanation. The main effects are higher pore-water pressure, which reduces the friction between grains, and the extra weight of the water.
items.correction_markdown: Write that water raises pore-water pressure, lowers strength and adds weight.

items.erreur_markdown: Prevention: plant trees and build walls.
items.pourquoi_faux: A list of methods without a mechanism earns little credit, and it does not show that you understand why each measure works.
items.correction_markdown: Write that tree roots bind soil and reduce infiltration, and that a retaining wall resists the downslope force on the slope behind it.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the type of mass movement in each case. (a) A slab of rock slides over a bedding plane that dips out of the slope. (b) A block moves on a curved surface and leaves a crescent-shaped scarp at the top. (c) Leaning poles and bent tree trunks are found on a gentle slope, with no sudden failure.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Rock slide (translational slide)**: movement along a flat plane of weakness. (b) **Rotational slump**: movement on a curved surface with backward tilting and a scarp. (c) **Soil creep**: very slow surface movement. Award a mark for each correct name.

items.enonce_markdown: A rock slab of weight 6000 kN rests on a plane inclined at 25 degrees. The base area is 80 m$^2$, the cohesion is 8 kPa and the friction angle is 28 degrees. (a) Calculate the factor of safety when the plane is dry. (b) After heavy rain, water pressure produces an uplift force of 2200 kN on the base. Calculate the new factor of safety. (c) State whether the slab is stable in each case. Use $FS = \dfrac{cA + (W\cos\theta - U)\tan\varphi}{W\sin\theta}$.
items.solution_markdown:
Driving force: $W\sin\theta = 6000\sin 25^\circ = 2536$ kN. Cohesion term: $cA = 8 \times 80 = 640$ kN. Normal force: $W\cos\theta = 5438$ kN.

(a) Dry: $FS = \dfrac{640 + 5438 \tan 28^\circ}{2536} = \dfrac{3531}{2536} = $ **1.39**.

(b) Wet: $FS = \dfrac{640 + (5438 - 2200)\tan 28^\circ}{2536} = \dfrac{2362}{2536} = $ **0.93**.

(c) The dry slab has $FS > 1$ and is **stable**; the wet slab has $FS < 1$ and is **unstable**, because the uplift cancels part of the normal force and lowers the frictional resistance.

items.enonce_markdown: A hillside settlement is exposed to landslides. Discuss whether engineering structures or education combined with early warning and land-use planning give the better protection for the lives of residents, and reach a justified conclusion. (8 marks)
items.solution_markdown: **Conclusion: education, warning and planning protect lives more reliably across the settlement, but engineering is still needed at critical sites.** Award a mark for each of the following, up to 8. Structures such as retaining walls, drains and rock bolts lower the chance of failure on one slope (1). They are costly and need maintenance (1), protect only the slope where they are built (1) and can be overwhelmed by an extreme storm (1). Education teaches residents to recognise warning signs such as new cracks, leaning trees and muddy springs (1). Early warning and evacuation move people out before failure (1). Zoning keeps houses off steep and unstable ground, a lasting reduction in exposure (1). These measures can be applied across a whole district (1). A reasoned conclusion that roads and key buildings which cannot move still need engineering earns a further mark (1).

items_markdown: Mass movement is the downslope movement of rock, regolith or soil under gravity, with no river or glacier carrying it.
The main types are rockfall, rock slide, rotational slump, debris flow or mudflow and soil creep.
Slope stability is the factor of safety, resisting force divided by driving force, and failure occurs when it falls below 1.
Water is the usual trigger: it raises pore-water pressure, lowers friction and adds weight.
Prevention reduces the chance of failure; minimising impacts reduces exposure through zoning, warning and education.
In prevention answers, name each method and say how it works.
